overview.intro:
Chapter 46 covers goods made from **plaiting materials** — straw, osier or willow, bamboo, rattan, rushes, reeds, seagrass, water hyacinth, raffia, strips of wood or paper and plastic strip over 5 mm wide. Heading 4601 holds plaits, mats, matting and screens; heading 4602 holds **baskets, wickerwork, bags and other articles** made directly to shape, plus articles of loofah. Its **49 tariff lines** run from Free (wickerwork and floor coverings) to 18% (palm-leaf handbags); most baskets pay 4.5%–10%.

The extra duty by country decides the cost. Since **July 24, 2026** goods from 60 economies pay a **Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5%** — **12.5% from Vietnam, the Philippines and Thailand**, 10% from India and Indonesia — and no Chapter 46 line is on the general exemption list. Rattan goods from Indonesia, Cambodia and nine other countries are exempt through their country exception lists. China pays **37.5% more** (25% List 3 + 12.5%) on every line. USMCA-qualifying goods from Mexico enter free; Canada pays a **50% Section 338 duty** on 4602.19.80. U.S. imports were **$614M in 2025**, led by Vietnam (25%), China (21%) and India (20%).

workedExamples.title: Water hyacinth storage baskets from Vietnam
workedExamples.body: Baskets woven from water hyacinth are not wickerwork — CBP limits that to rods and twigs with a round cross section (HQ H263914) — so they fall in 4602.19.18 at 4.5% (NY N336147). Vietnam's Section 301 rate adds 12.5% (9903.05.84): a $10,000 shipment pays **$1,700**. No exception list covers this line.

workedExamples.title: Rattan baskets: China vs Indonesia vs Vietnam
workedExamples.body: Rattan baskets that are not wickerwork pay 5%. From China, List 3 (+25%, 9903.88.03) and the 2026 action (+12.5%, 9903.05.31) stack: **$4,250** on $10,000. From Indonesia only the base rate applies, **$500**, because 4602.12 is on Indonesia's exception list (U.S. note 52(j)(11), 9903.06.16). From Vietnam: 5% + 12.5% = **$1,750**.

workedExamples.title: Raffia handbags from Madagascar, with an AGOA claim
workedExamples.body: CBP classifies raffia handbags as palm-leaf handbags in 4602.19.25, 18% (HQ H284742). Madagascar is not one of the 60 Section 301 economies, and AGOA (SPI D, renewed through December 31, 2026) makes the line Free: **$0** on $10,000 when the bags meet the AGOA origin rules. The same bags from China pay 55.5% ($5,550), from the Philippines 30.5%.

workedExamples.title: Decorative plaited articles from Canada vs Mexico
workedExamples.body: Other articles of vegetable plaiting materials (decorative figures, loofah articles) are 2.3%. From Canada, 4602.19.80 is on the Section 338 list in U.S. note 51(b)(1) (9903.03.12), charged even when USMCA is claimed: **$2,500** on a $5,000 shipment entered since August 22, 2026. From Mexico with a USMCA claim: **$0**.

notes.chapterNotes:
**Note 1.** In this chapter the expression "plaiting materials" means materials in a state or form suitable for plaiting, interlacing or similar processes; it includes straw, osier or willow, bamboos, rattans, rushes, reeds, strips of wood, strips of other vegetable material (for example, strips of bark, narrow leaves and raffia or other strips obtained from broad leaves), unspun natural textile fibers, monofilament and strip and the like of plastics and strips of paper, but not strips of leather or composition leather or of felt or nonwovens, human hair, horsehair, textile rovings or yarns, or monofilament and strip and the like of chapter 54.

**Note 2.** This chapter does not cover: (a) wall coverings of heading 4814; (b) twine, cordage, ropes or cables, plaited or not (heading 5607); (c) footwear or headgear or parts thereof of chapter 64 or 65; (d) vehicles or bodies for vehicles of basketware (chapter 87); or (e) articles of chapter 94 (for example, furniture, luminaires and lighting fittings).

**Note 3.** For the purposes of heading 4601, the expression "plaiting materials, plaits and similar products of plaiting materials, bound together in parallel strands" means plaiting materials, plaits and similar products of plaiting materials, placed side by side and bound together, in the form of sheets, whether or not the binding materials are of spun textile materials.

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares two editions of the tariff schedule: the **2025 Basic Edition**, in force at the start of 2025, and the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026). All 49 Chapter 46 lines carry the same base rates in both.

What changed came on top of the base rate. In 2025 the IEEPA tariffs added 20% on Vietnamese and 19% on Philippine, Indonesian, Thai and Cambodian baskets, 25%–50% on Indian goods and 20%–30% more on Chinese goods. They **ended on February 24, 2026**, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge that replaced them expired on July 23, 2026. Since **July 24, 2026**, goods from 60 economies pay a **Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5%**; rattan goods from 11 countries are exempt. China keeps its 25% List 3 duty, and since **August 22, 2026 Canada pays 50%** under Section 338 on 4602.19.80, USMCA claim or not.
tariffUpdates.scope: Measures that reach Chapter 46 from any country: the 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies and their country exception lists, the Brazil Section 301 tariff, China Section 301 List 3, the Canada Section 338 duty, the Nicaragua Section 301 phase-in, and the 2025–2026 IEEPA and Section 122 duties that have ended; plus the Lacey Act plant declaration that reaches most vegetable-material lines. No antidumping or countervailing duty order and no Section 232 action covers a Chapter 46 line. For the rate each supplier pays, see Rates by country.

understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 46 goods fell from **$651M in 2024 to $614M in 2025** (−5.7%), well below the 2021–2022 peak of about $875M. Almost all of it — **$594M, 97%** — is heading 4602: baskets and articles of other vegetable materials such as seagrass, water hyacinth, willow and palm leaf (4602.19, $273M), articles of plastic or paper strip (4602.90, $217M, down 13%), rattan ($53M, +6%) and bamboo ($52M). Mats, plaits and screens of heading 4601 were only $19M.

**Vietnam became the largest supplier**, $154M (25%, +8.6%), as **China fell 22% to $131M** — down from $356M in 2021. India ($120M) fell 21%, while Mexico ($53M, +14.5%) and Thailand ($27M, +38.5%) grew. The Philippines ($35M) and Indonesia ($34M) were roughly flat; Italy, Madagascar and Cambodia each shipped $8M–$11M.

Through 2025 China paid its 25% List 3 duty plus the IEEPA duties, and most other suppliers paid the IEEPA reciprocal tariff from April 2025 (Vietnam 20%, the Philippines, Indonesia and Thailand 19% from August 7), while USMCA-qualifying Mexican goods paid nothing extra. Those duties ended on February 24, 2026; since July 24, 2026 a Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5% applies instead. 2025 is the latest full year of U.S. trade data.

The total rate on Chapter 46 goods depends far more on **where they come from** than on what they are made of. Each cell below is the base rate for that product group plus the extra duty for that country, minus any preference — computed from the current tariff schedule with the same engine as the tariff calculator.

tariffEngineering.h1: Importing Baskets, Wickerwork & Plaited Goods (HTS Ch. 46): Rules, Documents & Ways to Lower Duty

seo.title: Importing Baskets & Wickerwork: Lacey Act, APHIS, Classification & Ways to Lower Duty (HTS Ch. 46) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: The USDA and CBP rules for each HTS Chapter 46 line — Lacey Act declarations, APHIS inspection and treatment of wooden handicrafts from China, corn-husk and rice-straw quarantines, origin marking — and the legal ways to pay less: wickerwork classification, exception lists, USMCA, AGOA and FTAs, rulings and drawback.
keywords: lacey act compliance for hts chapter 46

tariffEngineering.intro:
Most Chapter 46 goods are plant material, so **USDA rules apply alongside the duty**: bamboo, rattan and most other vegetable-material lines need a **Lacey Act plant declaration**; baskets with wood, twigs, vines or bamboo are wooden handicrafts that APHIS inspects, and **from China they must be treated and tagged** with the maker's identity; corn-husk articles and rice straw are under quarantine rules.

The ways to pay less are in the schedule: get the **wickerwork** classification where it fits (Free instead of 4.5%–10%), source rattan goods from a country whose **exception list** covers them, claim **USMCA** on Mexican and Canadian goods, claim **AGOA or an FTA** where the base rate is the cost, get a **binding ruling** where the line decides the rate, and claim **drawback** on re-exports. Each depends on a document, listed below with its regulation.

levers.title: Classify true wickerwork in the Free wickerwork lines
levers.saves: The whole base rate: Free instead of 10% (bamboo baskets), 5% (rattan), 4.5% (other vegetable baskets), 6.6% (other articles) or 2.3%
levers.appliesTo: Baskets and articles of bamboo, rattan, willow, wood, palm leaf and other vegetable materials made of interlaced rods or twigs (4602.11.07, .35; 4602.12.14, .35; 4602.19.14, .17, .35, .60)
levers.document: Product specifications showing the plaiting material is in rod or twig form with a round cross section; a binding ruling if in doubt.
levers.caveat: CBP treats wickerwork as articles of interlaced rods or twigs with rounded cross sections; flat strips, split slats, water hyacinth or seagrass that flatten when woven are not wickerwork (HQ H263914). The Section 301 duty still applies to the value.

citations.label: CBP ruling HQ H263914 (wickerwork vs. water hyacinth baskets)

levers.title: Source rattan goods from a country whose exception list covers them
levers.appliesTo: Rattan mats, plaits and webbing, woven willow mats and rattan baskets and articles (4601.22, 4601.29.40, 4601.93, 4602.12) from Indonesia, Cambodia, Malaysia, Taiwan, Bangladesh, Argentina, Ecuador, Jordan, Guatemala, El Salvador or Switzerland
levers.document: Proof of origin for the country claimed (commercial invoice, certificate of origin, production records) and the country's exemption heading (for example 9903.06.16 for Indonesia) on the entry line.
levers.caveat: Origin follows where the basket is made; CBP found baskets woven in Vietnam from Vietnamese seagrass and water hyacinth to be of Vietnamese origin (NY N354847). Transshipment does not change origin. China is on no exception list.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(j)
CBP ruling NY N354847 (origin of seagrass and water hyacinth baskets)

levers.title: Claim USMCA on baskets made in Mexico or Canada
levers.saves: The 10% Section 301 duty for Mexico or Canada plus the base rate (up to 18%)
levers.appliesTo: All 49 lines, for goods that qualify as originating under USMCA
levers.document: A certification of origin from the importer, exporter or producer, in any format. Heading 4601 goods must change from any other chapter and heading 4602 goods from any other heading (General Note 11), so baskets woven in Mexico from imported plaiting materials qualify.
levers.caveat: For Canada, USMCA does not remove the 50% Section 338 duty on 4602.19.80 (U.S. note 51(a)). The USMCA was not renewed at the July 1, 2026 joint review but remains in force.

citations.label: USTR statement on the USMCA joint review (July 1, 2026)

levers.title: Claim AGOA or an FTA rate where the base rate is the cost
levers.saves: The base rate: up to 18% on handbags, 10% on bamboo baskets, 4.5%–6.6% on most others
levers.appliesTo: The 36 dutiable lines, for goods of AGOA countries such as Madagascar (through December 31, 2026), CAFTA-DR, Australia, Chile, Colombia, Peru, Panama, Korea, Israel, Jordan, Morocco, Bahrain, Oman, Singapore and CBERA countries
levers.document: Proof of origin under the program and the SPI on the entry line (D for AGOA, P, AU, CL, CO, … , E for CBERA).
levers.caveat: FTA claims do not remove the 2026 Section 301 duty (U.S. note 52(a)); Madagascar is not one of the 60 economies, so its AGOA goods pay nothing. GSP (A, A*, A+) has been expired since December 31, 2020.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(a)

levers.title: Get a binding ruling before you import
levers.saves: Certainty where the line decides the rate: wickerwork (Free) vs. other baskets; plaited bags (4602) vs. handbags of chapter 42; plastic strip over 5 mm (4602.90, 3.5%) vs. textile strip (chapters 54 and 63); rope-coiled baskets (6307); rattan furniture (chapter 94)
levers.appliesTo: Any line where classification is in doubt — especially composite baskets with metal frames or textile liners
levers.document: A ruling request to CBP describing the product, its materials and construction (19 CFR part 177). Published rulings such as N336147 (water hyacinth basket), H284742 (raffia handbags), N307583 (loofah sponge), N355878 (polypropylene strip bag) and H342184 (rope baskets) show how CBP decides.
levers.caveat: Rulings apply to the transaction described; a different product may need its own.

citations.label: CBP ruling NY N355878 (strip width and Chapter 46)

levers.title: Claim drawback when the goods are exported
levers.saves: Up to 99% of the duties paid, including Section 301 duties, on imported goods re-exported or used in exported goods
levers.appliesTo: All lines, when the imported goods or substitutes are exported or used in manufacturing exported goods (for example gift baskets assembled for export)
levers.document: A drawback claim filed in ACE within 5 years of import, with records linking the import to the export.
levers.caveat: Only duties actually paid are refunded; manufacturing drawback needs a ruling or a general manufacturing ruling.

rules.title: Lacey Act plant declaration (genus, species, country of harvest, quantity, value) for 4601.21–4601.94, 4602.11, 4602.12 and 4602.19.05, .12, .35, .45, .60 and .80 — Phase VII, from December 1, 2024

Baskets and other wooden handicrafts (wood, twigs, vines, bamboo) are regulated articles inspected at the port of first arrival; from China, pieces over 1 cm in diameter must be treated and every package tagged with the manufacturer's identity
Articles of corn stalks, leaves or husks enter only if processed so that the inspector finds no pest risk (corn and broomcorn quarantine)
Rice straw and rice hulls are restricted from all foreign locations; APHIS may allow them only under a controlled import permit
Country-of-origin marking on each article (or its container when the article cannot be marked), in English
Wood pallets and crates must be ISPM 15 treated and marked; rice straw, bamboo leaves and other plant leaves used as packing are restricted

groups.label: Plaits, mats, matting and screens of plaiting materials (bamboo, rattan, willow, seagrass, plastic strip)
groups.note: Every vegetable-material mat and plait line (4601.21–4601.94) needs a Lacey Act declaration. Bamboo, willow and wood mats are wooden handicrafts that APHIS inspects; from China they must be treated and tagged.

groups.label: Baskets, wickerwork, bags and other articles of plaiting materials; articles of loofah
groups.note: Bamboo and rattan baskets, willow baskets and most other vegetable-material articles need a Lacey Act declaration; baskets and bags of palm leaf and other materials (4602.19.14–.18), handbags and luggage (4602.19.22–.29), 4601.99 and plastic-strip articles (4602.90) do not. Baskets of wood, twigs, vines or bamboo from China must be treated and tagged.

finalConclusion.intro: Straight answers to the most common questions about importing baskets, wickerwork, mats and other plaited goods into the U.S. — HS codes, tariffs by country and entry rules. Each answer links to the page with the full detail.
keyTakeaways: Chapter 46 base rates run from Free (wickerwork, floor coverings) to 18% (palm-leaf handbags); most baskets pay 4.5%–10%. None changed since January 2025.

faqs.question: What is basketware and wickerwork (HTS Chapter 46)?
faqs.answer: Chapter 46 covers goods made from plaiting materials — straw, osier or willow, bamboo, rattan, rushes, reeds, seagrass, raffia, strips of wood or paper and plastic strip. Heading 4601 is plaits, mats, matting and screens; heading 4602 is baskets, wickerwork, bags and other articles made directly to shape, plus articles of loofah. Furniture (chapter 94), hats (chapter 65), footwear, rope (5607) and wall coverings are excluded.

faqs.question: What does HS code 4602 cover?
faqs.answer: Basketwork, wickerwork and other articles made directly to shape from plaiting materials, and articles of loofah: 4602.11 of bamboo, 4602.12 of rattan, 4602.19 of other vegetable materials (willow, palm leaf, seagrass, water hyacinth, straw) and 4602.90 of non-vegetable materials such as plastic or paper strip (3.5%). Wickerwork lines are Free; other baskets pay 4.5%–10% and handbags up to 18%. 4602 was 97% of Chapter 46 imports in 2025 ($594M).

faqs.question: What does HS code 4601 cover?
faqs.answer: Plaits and similar products of plaiting materials in strips, and mats, matting and screens: 4601.21 of bamboo, 4601.22 of rattan, 4601.29 of other vegetable materials, and 4601.92–4601.99 for other plaited products. Floor coverings are Free, woven mats 3.3%–4.8% and other mats 8% — CBP put bamboo placemats in 4601.21.90 at 8% (NY N236787).

faqs.question: What is the HS code for wicker, woven or storage baskets?
faqs.answer: It depends on the material: bamboo baskets 4602.11, rattan 4602.12, willow 4602.19.12, other vegetable materials such as seagrass, water hyacinth or straw 4602.19.17/.18, and plastic or paper strip 4602.90. Wickerwork of rods or twigs is Free; other baskets pay 4.5%–10% plus the country's extra duty. Baskets that are not plaited are elsewhere: rope-coiled textile baskets 6307.90 (HQ H342184) and iron wire baskets 7323.99 (NY N344719).

faqs.question: What counts as wickerwork, and why does it matter?
faqs.answer: CBP treats wickerwork as articles of interlaced rods or twigs with a round cross section, such as willow or vine. Wickerwork baskets are Free at the general rate, while other baskets of the same material pay 4.5%–10%. Baskets of flat strips, split slats, seagrass or water hyacinth stems that flatten when woven are not wickerwork (HQ H263914). The Section 301 duty applies either way.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for seagrass and water hyacinth baskets?
faqs.answer: Seagrass and water hyacinth baskets are 4602.19.18, 4.5% (NY N300305, N336147; HQ H263914). From Vietnam they pay 17% in total, from the Philippines or Thailand 17%, from India or Indonesia 14.5% and from China 42%. Composite baskets with a metal frame stay in 4602 when the plaiting material gives the essential character.

faqs.question: What is the HS code and tariff for rattan baskets?
faqs.answer: Rattan baskets and bags are 4602.12: wickerwork Free, other baskets 5%, handbags 9% or 18%, other articles 6.6%. From Indonesia, Cambodia, Malaysia, Taiwan and seven other countries rattan goods pay only the base rate (note 52(j) exception lists); from Vietnam the base rate plus 12.5%; from China plus 37.5% — 42.5% on a 5% basket.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for bamboo baskets and bamboo products?
faqs.answer: Bamboo baskets and bags are 4602.11 (wickerwork Free, others 10%), bamboo luggage and handbags 4602.11.21 (6.2%), and bamboo mats 4601.21. Raw bamboo poles are 1401.10 and bamboo furniture chapter 94. From China, a 10% bamboo basket pays 47.5% in total; bamboo baskets from China must also be treated and tagged under APHIS's wooden handicraft rule.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for rattan or wicker furniture?
faqs.answer: Not Chapter 46 — note 2(e) sends furniture to chapter 94: rattan seats 9401.53, bamboo seats 9401.52, rattan furniture 9403.83, bamboo furniture 9403.82 and furniture of cane or osier 9403.89.30. All are Free at the general rate, so the cost is the country's extra duty.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for loofah sponges?
faqs.answer: Heading 4602 names articles of loofah. CBP classified a natural loofah sponge in 4602.19.80, 2.3% (NY N307583). From Canada that line pays the 50% Section 338 duty even with USMCA; from Vietnam or the Philippines 14.8%; from China 39.8%.

faqs.question: How are straw, raffia and woven plastic bags classified?
searchedAs: hs code for pp woven bags
faqs.answer: Raffia handbags are palm-leaf handbags in 4602.19.25, 18% (HQ H284742). Bags woven to shape from plastic strip over 5 mm wide are 4602.90, 3.5% (NY N363965); strip 5 mm or narrower is a textile, and a bag of it went to 6305.33 (NY N355878). Handbags with an outer surface of textile or plastic sheeting are chapter 42.

faqs.question: What tariffs apply to baskets and wickerwork from China?
searchedAs: china tariff on basketware and wickerwork
faqs.answer: Every Chapter 46 line is on China Section 301 List 3 (+25%, 9903.88.03), and the 2026 Section 301 action adds +12.5% (9903.05.31): 37.5% on wickerwork, 42% on seagrass baskets, 42.5% on rattan baskets, 47.5% on bamboo baskets. No exclusion now in effect covers a Chapter 46 product. The IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026.

faqs.question: What tariffs apply to baskets from Vietnam, the Philippines and Indonesia?
searchedAs: vietnam tariff on basketware and wickerwork
faqs.answer: Since July 24, 2026: Vietnam and the Philippines pay the base rate plus 12.5% on every line (17% on a 4.5% seagrass basket); Indonesia pays plus 10%, except that its rattan goods (4601.22, 4601.29.40, 4601.93, 4602.12) pay only the base rate. Their 2025 IEEPA rates (20% Vietnam, 19% the Philippines and Indonesia) ended February 24, 2026.

faqs.question: Do baskets from Mexico and Canada pay tariffs?
faqs.answer: Not if they qualify for USMCA: heading 4602 goods must change from any other heading, so baskets woven in Mexico or Canada qualify even from imported plaiting materials. Qualifying goods pay no base rate and no Section 301 duty. The exception is Canadian 4602.19.80, which pays the 50% Section 338 duty even with USMCA. Without a claim, both countries pay the base rate plus 10%.

faqs.question: How many baskets does the U.S. import, and from where?
faqs.answer: $614M of Chapter 46 goods in 2025, down 5.7% from $651M in 2024. Vietnam supplied 25% ($154M), China 21% ($131M, down 22%), India 20% ($120M), Mexico 9%, and the Philippines and Indonesia about 5.5% each. Baskets of other vegetable materials (4602.19) were $273M and plastic-strip articles (4602.90) $217M.
